## Why

S660 (landed 2026-11-28) points the UI brief's CLI and TUI render commands at the renders directory (adj 667). Only the cloud claude UI pass can write there: `internal/daemon/runner.go:44-52` grants it, and `internal/engine/brief.go:234` shows the "renders directory is an exception" sentence only when `in.Vendor == "claude"` (adj 671, S648). A `claude-local`, `codex`, `codex-local` or `grok` UI pass is told to write files it cannot write (S648 finding 1).

Owner decisions, 2026-11-28 (adj 678 `ui.renders-dir-grant-vendors`, adj 679, adj 685 `ui.renders-dir-grant-codex`, adj 686 `ui.renders-dir-grant-grok`; Jon, session 8d711f67):
- `claude-local` gets the single-path write rule that `CloudUIAllowlist` gives cloud claude. Its permission mechanism is the approval hook plus `--allowedTools`.
- `codex` and `codex-local` keep the worktree read-only and get the renders directory as their only writable root. The implementer first probes the installed codex for a setting that does this and saves the probe under `testdata/vendors/codex/`. If codex has no such setting, the implementer stops, reports, and does not widen the grant. Mind GOCACHE under TEMP: ork sets `GOCACHE` to `TempDir/gocache` (`codexEnv`), so the probe must show whether `go test` still runs under the narrow grant.
- `grok` and `grok-local` are deferred (grok ends 2026-12-09). Their brief keeps the vendor gate, and the S648 lint row omits them.

The renders-directory sentence then shows for `claude`, `claude-local`, `codex` and `codex-local`, and not for `grok` or `grok-local`.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-28: adj 678 (grant every UI vendor), adj 679 (narrow per-vendor grant), adj 685 (codex: probe first, stop and report if none), adj 686 (grok deferred, keeps the gate) and adj 687 (claude-local writes its whole temp directory, like cloud claude).
